title: Hardware Key Adapter: Terraform sketch + rollout notes
content:
Purpose:
This is a working sketch for a lightweight HSM/KMS adapter we can ship with Private deployments. The goal is to provide a minimal, auditable interface between Redwood Private control plane components and customer-managed HSMs (PKCS#11 / Cloud HSM) such that secrets lifecycle + audit logs meet our enterprise compliance checklist without forcing Vault as a hard dependency.

Scope and constraints:
- Target customers: on-prem or VPC customers who require FIPS-friendly key material or HSM-backed wrapping keys.
- Must support: PKCS#11-compatible HSMs (Thales, YubiHSM, SoftHSM for dev), AWS CloudHSM, Azure Dedicated HSM where possible.
- Minimal runtime: an adapter service (daemon) that exposes a TLS JSON-RPC (gRPC optional) over a localhost unix-socket or mTLS endpoint in the customer's VPC.
- Terraform-first: provide modules to provision adapter resources, connection secrets, and RBAC for Redwood Private components.
- No implicit storage of unwrapped key material in Redwood control plane. Only key handles / wrapped keys are stored; HSM holds unwrap keys.

High-level design notes (sketch):
- Adapter responsibilities:
  - Key creation requests: create asymmetric keys inside HSM and return public key + key identifier (handle).
  - Data key wrapping: provide Encrypt/Decrypt or Wrap/Unwrap primitives for symmetric data keys used by services. The adapter must return wrapped keys and tokenized metadata (algorithm, KMS key id, version).
  - Key rotation orchestration: expose endpoints to schedule rotations and run migration of wrapped keys.
  - Audit logs: emit structured audit events to a local file and to a remote syslog/secure ELK endpoint. Events must include requestor identity (mTLS client cert CN), action, key-id, result, and a monotonic operation id.
  - Admin UI endpoint (optional): basic health + key list (no secret material) for on-prem SREs.

- Security model:
  - mTLS mandatory for control-plane <-> adapter comms, client cert pinned by Terraform-provisioned CA.
  - Least-privilege service accounts in K8s: if adapter runs in a customer's cluster, it must use PSP/PodSecurity and RBAC constraints; if run on a VM, systemd unit must drop privileges.
  - Wrap-only mode: support a mode where Redwood control plane never requests raw decrypt; only Wrap/Unwrap by customer orchestration.

Terraform module notes (inputs/outputs and behavior):
- Module: redwood/private-hsm-adapter (sketch)
  - Inputs (strings): adapter_name, env (prod|staging|dev), hsm_type (pkcs11|aws|azure|soft), hsm_endpoint, pkcs11_lib_path (optional), admin_principals (list of strings as cert CNs), audit_sink_url (optional)
  - Inputs (sensitive strings): adapter_tls_private_key, adapter_tls_cert, hsm_admin_token (if cloud hsm), customer_kms_config_json (blob)
  - Outputs (strings): adapter_endpoint, adapter_ca_cert, adapter_service_account_email, audit_bucket_path
  - Behavior notes: module should create TLS secret for adapter, create CA if not provided, configure k8s service account + rolebinding (if k8s target), optionally provision cloud-hsm client resources for AWS/Azure where permitted.

Terraform upgrade/migration plan (major steps):
1) v0.1: minimal module that deploys adapter as sidecar/daemonset in customer's cluster and configures TLS via supplied certs. No auto-provisioning of cloud HSM resources.
2) v0.2: add CloudHSM client hooks, documented IAM perm requirements (e.g., AWS CloudHSM client in VPC).
3) v0.3: add wrapped-key migration helper and rotation controller (Kubernetes Operator optional).
4) v1.0: formalize audit log shipment, HA adapter topology, and include full test harness.

Rollout checklist (short):
- Preflight (customer): HSM reachable from control plane subnets, customer agrees to adapter cert management, network security groups allow mTLS port (default 8443), SIEM endpoint info available.
- Provision (terraform): apply module with test key creation enabled, gather adapter_endpoint and adapter_ca_cert, push certs to Redwood Private control plane.
- Smoke tests: create test asymmetric key in HSM via adapter; sign/verify a blob; wrap/unwarp a sample data key.
- Audit verification: confirm adapter emits an event for each API call and that events contain client cert CN + non-sensitive meta.
- Canary rollout: enable adapter for a single tenant workload, monitor 72h, check latency/throughput and logs.
- Promote: expand to additional workloads, increase concurrency limits.

Operational runbook snippets (commands and checks):
- Health check (adapter running locally): curl --cacert adapter_ca.pem --cert client.pem --key client.key https://localhost:8443/health
- Test wrap: curl -X POST --cacert adapter_ca.pem --cert client.pem --key client.key https://adapter:8443/v1/wrap -d '{"plain_key":"...base64...","algorithm":"AES-GCM-256","key_id":"temp-key-1"}'
- Inspect logs: sudo tail -n 500 /var/log/redwood-hsm-adapter.log | jq '. | select(.event=="wrap")'
- Audit verify: grep operation_id /var/log/redwood-hsm-adapter-audit.jsonl | head -n 10

Audit schema (line-delimited JSON):
- timestamp: ISO8601
- operation_id: UUID
- requestor: client_cert_cn
- action: create_key|wrap|unwrap|rotate|list|health
- key_id: string or null
- result: success|failure
- error_code: string or null
- agent_version: semver
- request_meta: string (short blob — caller ip, request id)

Secrets handling and rotation model (recommendation):
- Never persist unwrapped symmetric data keys outside memory in control plane services. Wrapped data keys (ciphertext) may be persisted alongside metadata (key_id, algorithm, version).
- Rotation policy: maintain two active versions for each customer key: active and prev. Rotation controller performs: generate new data key, encrypt with new KMS key handle, re-encrypt persisted values (background migration) and mark previous version for TTL-based deletion after N days (configurable).
- Emergency rotation: support offline key rewrap given HSM-admin approval. Provide a manual CLI that creates a rotated key and produces a signed rotation proposal that requires two operator confirmations (key ceremony-lite).

Testing matrix and acceptance criteria:
- Functional: create/wrap/unwrap across supported HSM types; adapter gracefully fails if HSM latency > threshold.
- Security: mTLS enforced; cert revocation enforced via CRL or short-lived certs; audit events present for all operations.
- Performance: 95th percentile wrap latency < 50ms in colocated setups; tail latency < 200ms. Document observed metrics per HSM type in a follow-up doc.
- Upgrade: terraform module applies without recreating adapter container for non-breaking changes; breaking changes must be gated behind a feature flag.

Open questions / TODOs (short list):
- Certificate management: should we integrate with our existing PKI operator or expect customers to supply certs? Decision needed before v0.1.
- HSM vendor SDK licensing: confirm redistribution policy for vendor libs (PKCS#11 .so) inside adapter container image.
- Sync with SRE on audit retention policy and SIEM ingestion format (JSONL vs GELF).

Notes to reviewers (informal):
- This document intentionally keeps the adapter lightweight; we want to avoid forcing Vault as the only supported path. Our customers frequently have their own key ceremony processes and will prefer an adapter they can control.
- Aim to ship a beta that is easy to run in an air-gapped environment (SoftHSM for test + clear instructions for swapping in vendor libs).

Appendix: example minimal Terraform usage (sketch):
module "hsm_adapter" {
  source = "github.com/redwood-inference/modules//private-hsm-adapter"
  adapter_name = "redwood-hsm-adapter-prod"
  env = "prod"
  hsm_type = "pkcs11"
  pkcs11_lib_path = "/opt/yubihsm/libyubihsm.so"
  admin_principals = ["redwood-controlplane-cn"]
  adapter_tls_cert = file("./secrets/adapter.crt")
  adapter_tls_private_key = file("./secrets/adapter.key")
}

End of sketch.

Change log (mini):
- 2024-09-18: initial sketch created by Asha.
- 2024-10-03: added terraform inputs/outputs and upgrade plan; flagged open questions.
